text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opposition in opening and closing","quality":"thesis consistency","description":"The essay keeps a steady position against driverless cars and returns to that claim at the end, which makes its argument easier to follow."},{"evidence":"“you still need to be alert…,” “driving… developes certain skills”","quality":"reasoned support","description":"It gives several linked reasons for its position, including safety, skill-building, and responsibility, rather than mostly repeating approval."},{"evidence":"“if there is any malfunction, everyone would just blame the car”","quality":"counterargument handling","description":"The essay acknowledges the other side and then answers it, which strengthens the persuasiveness of the argument."},{"evidence":"“drunk and don't want to call a cab,” “quick nap on the way to work”","quality":"concrete examples","description":"It uses specific everyday examples to make the argument feel more realistic and grounded."},{"evidence":"organized body paragraphs with intro, concession, rebuttal, conclusion","quality":"organization","description":"The essay has a clearer argumentative structure, with the claim, supporting points, opposing view, and wrap-up separated in a logical order."}]}
